sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
MOUSE at (50,30) had an effect (no_impact: False) but the upper area didn't change. Looking at the ASCII: the top-center cell of the 3x3 checker tile changed from W to N! Row 52: `GGgggGGNNNGGgggGG` — the top-center of the right tile is now N (light green) instead of W. So clicking the white cell of the checker tile changed its color from W→N!
This is a big discovery: the bottom tiles are interactive! Clicking a white cell turns it light green (N).
So the game is: the bottom tiles are a "goal board" that you fill in by moving the puck? The 3x3 checker has white cells at N, W, E, S (edge centers). Clicking one turns it green.
Hmm, wait, but why would clicking a goal cell turn it green? Maybe the goal is to turn all the white cells green, and the way to do it is... by clicking? But that's too easy — you could just click all 4 white cells.
Or maybe clicking is just a "test" and the real mechanic is: the puck's orientation determines which cell gets filled, and the cells get filled when the puck is docked in the correct orientation.
Actually, wait — let me reconsider. Maybe the bottom-right tile is a "scoreboard"/progress display: a 3x3 grid where you need to fill the 4 edge cells (N, W, E, S) with green. And the way to fill them is: dock the puck at the corner of the track with the b half facing that direction! The 4 directions = the 4 white cells. The purple plus tile (bottom-left) shows the plus shape = the 4 edge cells (N, W, E, S) — that's the "goal pattern" legend!
So: the goal is to fill all 4 edge cells of the 3x3 grid. Each is filled by docking the puck at the corner with the b half facing that direction (up, down, left, right). My mouse click accidentally turned the N cell green (or maybe clicking is a valid way to fill it too? That would be weird).
Hmm, but if clicking directly fills cells, then the puzzle is trivial (click 3 more times). But maybe clicking is just a "preview" and the cell only stays green if... let me check: is the N cell still green? Yes, in the current frame it's N.
Wait, maybe clicking the white cell is actually a legitimate mechanic: the mouse is a "painter"? But then why have the puck?
Let me think from another angle: maybe the game is "Simon"-like: the puck's orientation must match... hmm.
Actually, let me test: dock the puck at the corner with b facing left (LEFT), and see if the W cell of the checker turns green. If so, the mechanic is confirmed: dock + orientation fills the corresponding cell. And the mouse click might have been a "cheat" that also fills (or maybe the click did something else entirely — like selecting the tile).
Wait, actually, the click might have done something else: maybe clicking the tile toggles a "target mode" and the N cell turned green because... hmm, the N cell was W (white). Now it's N (light green). The timer bar is also N (light green). Interesting: the timer color is N.
Let me test the dock hypothesis: press LEFT until the puck docks at c23-26 (b facing left), and check whether the W cell (row 56, column 27?) turns green.
Checker tile: rows 51-64, columns 27-40. 3x3 cells: each cell is about 4-5px. From the ASCII: row 52: `GGgggGGNNNGGgggGG` at columns 27-40: G G g g g G G N N N G G g g g G G. So the top row of cells: [ggg][NNN][ggg] — the top-center cell is now NNN (3x3? rows 52-54, columns 34-36). The white cells are: top-center (rows 52-54, columns 34-36), middle-left (rows 56-58, columns 28-30), middle-right (rows 56-58, columns 38-40), bottom-center (rows 60-62, columns 34-36).
So the W cell = rows 56-58, columns 28-30.
Test: LEFT (dock the puck, b facing left), then check whether the W cell changed.
